newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian auto firm plans faster growth.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian auto firm plans faster growth.

text.p: Three months after the death of its chairman raised concerns about its future, Malaysian conglomerate DRB-Hicom group is looking to expand through acquisitions.

The group will retain its focus in automobile, finance and construction sectors, but plans to speed up growth as Malaysia moves closer to opening its markets under various international agreements, new chairman Saleh Sulong said in an interview.
Saleh replaced Yahaya Ahmad, who was killed in a helicopter crash in March.
"We have to be more earnest in our endeavour to be prepared for the advent of AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area) by 2003 vis-a-vis our automotive business," Saleh told Reuters on Wednesday.

AFTA is being developed by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Cambodia, Laos and Burma are expected to join this year.
The group consists of automobile assembler Diversified Resources Bhd and the privatised automobile and engineering group Hicom Holdings Bhd.
Perhaps its best known company is Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton), which makes the national car.
DRB-Hicom also controls the construction firm Gadek Bhd KL, car distrbutor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd (EON) and cement maker Kedah Cement.
Saleh said the company was also involved in several projects of national interest.

They include the public transportation system for Kuala Lumpur, waste disposal management, a second national air carrier Air Asia, Kuala Lumpur airport services, the national motorcycle project, the national truck project and the national railway privatisation project.
"I will have to provide the necessary kind of leadership as to get everybody excited over things, the same way, if not better than the late Tan Sri (Yahaya)," he said.

Saleh said growth would be speeded up through acquisitions, new projects and fund-raising exercises. The group is looking for companies to buy in its core areas of construction, automobile and finance.
"We are looking at acquisitions with a view to expanding rapidly," he told Reuters.
"I wouldn't dismiss the possibility (of public issues) in the near future, bearing in mind the magnitude of the funding required," he said.

"Nevertheless, a sizeable portion of it (funds) will be coming from within because we have been registering good profit as of late. I think we will not be so much bogged down, or impeded too much by financial costs."
DRB and Hicom have yet to release their results for the year to March 31.
Proton, the company with the biggest revenues in the group, reported a 200 percent increase in its net profit to 344.55 million ringgit ($137.82 million) in the six months to September 30, 1996.
For the same period, DRB announced a 95-percent increase in net profit to 61.39 million ringgit over the year-ago period. ($1=2.5 ringgit).
